cls: Androgen (esterified testosterone, short-acting steroid hormone) - Controlled Substance Schedule III (anabolic steroid)
quick: Male hypogonadism: 25-50 mg IM 2-3 times weekly
Not applicable - administered by deep intramuscular injection
Contraindicated - causes virilization of female fetus (Category X)
Contraindicated; may pass into milk and suppress lactation
Use with caution; fluid retention may worsen renal/cardiac disease
Caution; discontinue if cholestatic jaundice or liver dysfunction
No direct interaction; avoid hepatotoxic combinations
Serum testosterone, hematocrit, PSA, lipids, LFTs
summary: Testosterone propionate is a short-acting esterified androgen used as replacement therapy in males with confirmed hypogonadism (primary testicular failure or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism) and to stimulate puberty in delayed-puberty boys. As an anabolic-androgenic steroid it is a Schedule III controlled substance with abuse potential. Because of its short ester it requires frequent intramuscular injection. It carries risks of polycythemia, prostate effects, fluid retention, and virilization in females.
indications: Replacement therapy in males with primary hypogonadism (congenital or acquired testicular failure)
Replacement therapy in males with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (idiopathic or due to LHRH deficiency or pituitary-hypothalamic injury)
Delayed puberty in selected adolescent boys (short-term)

dosage.n: Deep intramuscular injection; titrate to serum testosterone
Short course (4-6 months); monitor bone age

admin: Administer by deep intramuscular injection only (do not give IV)
Short ester requires frequent dosing compared with longer-acting esters
Warm vial and inspect for crystals if oil-based; allow to reach room temperature
moa: Testosterone propionate is hydrolyzed to free testosterone, the principal endogenous androgen. It binds intracellular androgen receptors to regulate gene transcription, promoting development and maintenance of male secondary sexual characteristics, spermatogenesis support, nitrogen retention, protein anabolism, and erythropoiesis (via increased erythropoietin and direct marrow stimulation).

absolute: Known or suspected carcinoma of the prostate
Serious cardiac, hepatic, or renal disease

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy (Category X). Androgens cause virilization of the external genitalia of the female fetus, including clitoromegaly and labial fusion, with risk increasing with dose and trimester of exposure.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. Testosterone may be excreted in breast milk and may have adverse androgenic effects on the infant; high doses can also suppress milk production.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment. Androgens can cause sodium and fluid retention, which may worsen edema, hypertension, or renal/cardiac compromise. Serious renal disease is a contraindication.
hepatic: Use with caution; discontinue if cholestatic hepatitis with jaundice or abnormal liver function develops. Although hepatotoxicity is more characteristic of 17-alpha-alkylated oral androgens, esterified injectable testosterone should still be avoided in serious hepatic disease.

major: Oral anticoagulants/warfarin (potentiation of anticoagulant effect - increased bleeding risk; monitor INR)
moderate: Insulin and oral hypoglycemics (may reduce blood glucose, adjust antidiabetic dose)
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; avoid combining with other hepatotoxins
interactions.diagnostics: May decrease thyroxine-binding globulin and total T4; may alter metyrapone test and other endocrine tests

serious: Prostate enlargement/worsening of subclinical prostate cancer
Cardiovascular events (MI, stroke - associated with androgen use)
rare: Peliosis hepatis / hepatic neoplasms (more with oral alkylated androgens)
emergency: Pulmonary oil microembolism (cough, dyspnea, chest pain during/after injection)

monitoring: Hematocrit/hemoglobin at baseline and periodically (hold if elevated)
Prostate assessment (PSA and digital rectal exam) in older men
Signs of virilization in females exposed
counsel: This is a controlled substance (Schedule III) - do not share and store securely
Report difficulty breathing, chest pain, or leg swelling (clot risk)
Women who are or may become pregnant must avoid exposure to the drug
Report frequent or persistent erections, breast tenderness, or yellowing of skin/eyes
Regular blood tests and prostate checks are required
Do not exceed prescribed dose; misuse for muscle building is dangerous and illegal
pk: Begins after IM absorption and ester hydrolysis within hours to days
Serum testosterone peaks within ~1-2 days of injection
Short - effective duration of the propionate ester is roughly 1-3 days
Store at controlled room temperature 20-25 C; protect from light; do not freeze
pearls: Schedule III controlled substance (anabolic-androgenic steroid) with abuse potential
Shortest-acting common testosterone ester - frequent dosing needed versus enanthate/cypionate
Monitor hematocrit; discontinue or reduce if it rises above ~54% due to thrombosis risk
Suppresses endogenous gonadotropins and spermatogenesis - not for fertility
missed: If a scheduled injection is missed, administer it as soon as possible and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up to make up for a missed dose. Contact the prescriber if multiple doses are missed.
overdose: Acute overdose of injectable testosterone is unlikely to be life-threatening. Chronic excess or abuse causes polycythemia, hypertension, cardiomyopathy, hepatic effects, gonadal suppression, and aggression/mood changes. Management is discontinuation and supportive care; phlebotomy may be needed for marked polycythemia.
